data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold, and the RP2354B stays for "Microcontroller". The stock verifier refutes nothing. Its verdict is confirmed, its refutation text is empty and all 12 of its checks pass. The datasheet verifier fails 3 checks: watchdog stall cover (V2), watchdog window (V1 and V2) and image watchdog timeout (V4). I re-read the sources, and none of the 3 is a property of the part.

(1) What the part can do. RP2350 datasheet Table 1249 (LOAD, bits 23:0) allows a timeout up to 0xffffff us, "approximately 16 seconds". Table 1248 gives CTRL.ENABLE (bit 30) a reset value of 0x0, so firmware turns the watchdog on. Any timeout below V1's 500 ms (owner, 2026-09-30) can be set. So can any timeout above the 400 ms packaged-part maximum of one W25Q16JV sector erase. The datasheet does not state the time from expiry to the pads reaching their reset state. That time is not read.

(2) V2 and the window. The 900 ms stall is one erase followed by a console printf in the same main-loop pass (firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:1049-1089, re-read). With a slow host, pico-sdk's USB console write has no fixed bound. The erase in the loop and the uncapped console write are both choices in the firmware. Moving the store to the FRAM (Q8) and capping the write would remove them. No microcontroller's watchdog covers a stall that has no bound, so the missing window is a firmware gap, not a limit of this silicon.

(3) V4. `grep -rn -i watchdog firmware/ shared/` in checkout fe53d3a8bc9a finds only comments: main.c:970-973, firmware/panel/main/main.c:697 and shared/link/include/link_dev.h:6 and :87. It finds no watchdog_enable, watchdog_update or watchdog_reboot. So "none set" is the value found for V4. It is a firmware gap that IOBoard.md:251 already records ("The image enables none").

The RP2354B is also a fixed input of the Scope table. A fixed input is checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source. One that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. This ruling matches FU-A4 adjudicator-R1 (007) and FU-2A adjudicator-R1 (010), which ruled the same way on the same 3 checks.

Part-level facts I re-read all pass. JLCPCB C39843328 is the RP2354B (Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), SC1512(13)-A4), with stockCount 2540 and canPresaleNumber 2407. The PCN (product change notice) listing holds only "RP235x A4 stepping PCN", which ends the steppings other than A4. The 20 held parts cover the need of 10.

The scope is function, because the failed checks concern this function's V1, V2 and V4 values in the firmware. None concerns the lifecycle, an end-of-life notice, the maker allowlist or the LCSC identity. For the owner and firmware: the image sets no watchdog timeout, the cap on the console write is not stated, and the expiry-to-reset time is not measured.
data.evidence: RP2350 datasheet, served build (SHA-256 2877d0f270fb6d6a57943bee58aaad536aa027bea1e5b1c4ce2541a3230d4be8, 7,968,417 bytes; the same hash the verifier cites). Table 1248 CTRL: "30 ENABLE: When not enabled the watchdog timer is paused, RW, 0x0". Table 1249 LOAD: "23:0 Load the watchdog timer. The maximum setting is 0xffffff which corresponds to approximately 16 seconds." Checkout fe53d3a8bc9aa58f294eb764b16a73cbd3b2df43: grep -rn -i watchdog over firmware/ and shared/ finds comments only, at firmware/iomcu/src/main.c:970-973, firmware/panel/main/main.c:697 and shared/link/include/link_dev.h:6 and :87, with no watchdog API call. main.c:1049-1089 calls out_store_tick and out_store_reclaim (sector erase) and printf in the same loop pass. IOBoard.md:251: "The image enables none: no call to one appears under firmware/iomcu/". V1 = 500 ms (owner, 2026-09-30); V2 and V4 are for research (Research.md, Raised by P1). Scope table: a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. JLCPCB exact match C39843328: RP2354B, Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), SC1512(13)-A4, stockCount 2540, canPresaleNumber 2407, expand. The PCN listing (HTTP 200, 39,597 bytes) holds one notice, "RP235x A4 stepping PCN", updated 6 Oct 2025. Earlier rulings: round1/FU-A4/007-adjudicator-R1.json and round2/FU-2A/010-adjudicator-R1.json, both stands false, scope function, on the same watchdog checks. Not re-read: pico-sdk stdio_usb.c. The ruling does not depend on it, because the stall exists either way and is set by the firmware.
